bull.b: Currently low leverage reduces near-term solvency pressure and leaves more financial flexibility than a heavily indebted structure would. This can help Avalo preserve resources for clinical development and manage obligations while its pipeline remains commercially unproven.

A focused pipeline in immune-mediated and inflammatory diseases gives Avalo a defined development strategy rather than a broad, unfocused operating model. Successful clinical progress could create product or partnering opportunities, although programs remain investigational.

A substantially higher current equity base provides more balance-sheet support than Avalo had in earlier periods and may improve its capacity to fund development activities. This is a meaningful structural offset to losses, even though future financing needs remain possible.

bear.b: Sharp, sustained revenue contraction leaves Avalo with little commercial income to support operations and makes the business heavily dependent on advancing future products. Until revenue scales meaningfully, development spending is unlikely to be self-funded by the existing business.

Large recurring operating and net losses indicate that Avalo’s current activities are not yet economically self-sustaining. Persistently negative margins can consume capital over multiple periods and reduce flexibility to fund clinical programs, partnerships, or other strategic priorities.

Continued operating and free-cash-flow deficits mean Avalo is consuming cash rather than generating it from operations. Unless spending declines or revenue scales, ongoing development will require external funding, creating financing dependence and potential pressure on future capital allocation.
